newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela hopeful as heads for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Mandela hopeful as heads for Zaire talks.

text.p: South Africa's President Nelson Mandela left for Congo on Friday to host face-to-face peace talks between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, saying he was hopeful of success.

Mandela, who has staked his reputation to try to end the Zairean conflict, told reporters before departing for the Congolese port of Pointe-Noire that the rival leaders were keen to sort out their differences.

"Both President Mobutu and Mr Laurent Kabila are quite aware of the importance of this meeting," Mandela said before flying on the first leg of his journey to the South African naval ship off the Gabon coast where the talks are due to be held.
"I believe that each one of them will make an effort to find a settlement that is acceptable to both of them as well as the masses of the people in Zaire."

U.S., South African and United Nations mediators also gathered in the Angolan capital Luanda to prepare for the talks, which diplomatic sources said South Africa tried through the night to keep to the planned Friday start.
Mobutu has lost control of most of Africa's third largest country except the capital Kinshasa. Leaders of the seven-month rebellion have vowed to take the city if the talks make no progress.
